about: What lies under the reference game's deep place, below the bottom of what its makers made: the old dark they dug down to, or that came up to meet them (OR-1622: no level below the grave). One level more, of natural caves, written by the deep sites' own generator as the makers' levels are (src/world/deep/deep-below.ts): its rooms by role, its dwellers and its worst drawn for its depth, its treasure of the depth's tier, and in its den a warden lying on a hoard rolled on Deem's carried template. Each deep purpose says from which room of its bottom level the way down goes, in its own words (its `below`). Add a role, a scene or a warden to add a way; nothing in the engine needs to change.

names: a wet crawl under the flowstone

scenes: The crack comes down into a cleft of raw rock, no tool-mark on it anywhere. Water has worn it, long before anyone dug above. The air is still and colder than the rooms above.
You come down out of the crack onto a floor of wet stone. Above you the made walls end in a line as clean as a cut. Below it the rock is the mountain's own.
A cave too wide for your light, its roof hung with stone grown down in points. The floor is heaped with fallen slabs. Between them a path has been worn by feet that were not yours.
A cave the size of a hall, its floor a slope of rubble. Pale growths cover the stone in rings. Your steps come back to you from far off, a moment late.
A pool lies across the floor, black and perfectly still. Your light goes down into it and finds no bottom. Blind white fish turn away from it.
Water stands in a basin of flowstone, clear as air and very cold. Bones lie at the bottom, picked clean, of animals that came down to drink.
The floor drops into a pit full of bones, most of them gnawed. Among them lie the makers' dead, and older bones under those.
A hollow in the floor where bones have been thrown, or dragged, for longer than the works above have stood. Among them are buckles and rusted iron.
The cave pinches to a passage you must turn sideways to pass. The rock on either side is scored in long parallel lines, at the height of your head.
A low way between walls that almost meet. The floor is polished smooth, worn by a great weight dragged over it again and again.
A seam of crystal runs through the wall here, and your light comes back from it in a hundred colours. Pieces of it lie broken on the floor, prised out and dropped.
The wall of this cave is shot with a vein of pale stone that glitters. Long ago a miner tried to dig it out, and left a broken pick in the wall.
The narrows open into a round cave, warm, its floor scraped bare. The smell is thick here. At the far side the floor rises in a low heap that glints when your light touches it.
A dome of rock, dry and warm as a kitchen. The walls are blackened in streaks. In the middle of the floor lies a heap of old metal, worn into a hollow the shape of a sleeper.
